To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intracellular distribution of rotaviral proteins and VLPs is affected when they are coexpressed in insect cells.
rotavirus proteins and virus-like particle (VLP) accumulate in different locations in the cytoplams of insect cells.
the localization of recominant proteins and virus-like particle (VLP) assembly are different to those of the native virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the localization of rotavirus proteins in insect cells.
the assembly of rotavirus proteins expressed in insect cells and the production of RLP.
the intracellular localization of rotavirus proteins, and the assembly of RLP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VP6 and GFPVP2 form RLP in High Five cells.
the assembly of RLP occurs in the cytoplamic dense zone, and not in the ER.
the assembly of RLP is dependent of the protein composition of the particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intracellular localization of rotavirus structural recombinant proteins is different from the one observed for native virus.
slRLP accumulate in the cytoplamic as highly ordered aggregates while VP6 and VP6-GFPVP2 form fibrillar structures that are not associated to microtrubules.

the localization of rotavirus proteins expressed individually and in combination is different than that observed for the corresponding native proteins, and this could be related to the conditions of expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assembly of slRLP and of dlRLP are two different processes.
the assembly of recombinant VLP is a highly complex process and that the assembly of RLP in insect cells differs from the assembly of native virus.
, in the insect cell system, rotavirus-like particles assemble intracellularly and that the distribution of VP6 and GFPVP2 can be altered when they are coexpressed.
